title: Retain Font Attribute for Title

illustrates.quote: Follow print when a title is printed in italics or other emphasizing typeface and follows a preposition that is in a different typeface, or when the preposition is in a typeface different from the title.

blocks.features: Centered italic title (a complete heading on its own, per 5.3.5).
Centered subtitle: 'From' plain roman, book title 'Andrew Marvell Revisited' italic — the title follows a preposition in a different typeface, per 5.4.2's first clause.
Left-aligned, plain roman opening line of the poem (contrast Example 5-4, where the same line is italic).

print.notes: Same overall title-page layout as Example 5-4, but here the title is mentioned inside a subtitle ('From ... Revisited') rather than standing alone, so 5.4.2 (not 5.3.5) governs the referenced title's italics.
print.surroundingText: Follows rule 5.4.2 directly, on printed page 5-8.
print.printFeatures: Four centered/left lines, no border: italic main title, mixed-typeface subtitle, plain byline, plain poem line.

braille.notes: Seven lines, margin 8 stripped. Line 1 blank filler; line 2 centered title (indent 13), no typeform indicator, per 5.3.5; line 3 centered subtitle (indent 5) with a single-word italic indicator ('.7') before 'Andrew' and an italics terminator (".'") after 'Revisited' — 'f' (From) itself carries no italics marker, confirming only the title is italicized, matching print; line 4 blank (interior); line 5 centered byline (indent 12); line 6 blank (interior); line 7 flush-left poem line, no italics (matching plain print here, unlike Example 5-4).

resolution: Both runs agree on braille byte-for-byte and on the substantive print facts; only prose/heading-classification differed. Heading level (1, centered) verified directly against the (40−len)//2 formula for all three centered lines (title indent 13/len 13; subtitle indent 5/len 30; byline indent 12/len 16 — all match exactly), settling A's heading classification over B's flatter 'paragraph' choice with independent measurement, not either run's own account.
